newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Central Vietnam floods cause 72 deaths.
newsitem.headline: Central Vietnam floods cause 72 deaths.

text.p: Flooding in central and northern Vietnam has killed 72 people, bringing the nationwide toll from natural disasters over the last month to at least 230, relief authorities said on Friday.

The U.N.-sponsored Disaster Management Unit (DMU) said a succession of storms had destroyed or flooded thousands of homes in provinces from Thanh Hoa, near Hanoi in the north, to Danang and Kontum, about 600 km (400 miles) to the south.
Damage to the provinces, some of the poorest areas in the country, was estimated at close to $400 million.
The ancient imperial city of Hue, a major tourist destination, was submerged four times over the space of a month, the DMU said.
Rice fields and sugar cane plantations were also reported damaged, but the extent was unclear.

Vietnam has suffered a year of some of its worst natural disasters on record. The DMU said earlier this week that 162 people, most of them children, had died from continued flooding in southern Vietnam's Mekong Delta.
